newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends weaker,gives up week-long gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends weaker,gives up week-long gains.

text.p: The key three-month Euroyen futures contract on TIFFE ended weaker on Tuesday mainly due to profit taking, giving up all the gains it had accumulated in the past week, traders said.
"The March had been on the advance for no good reason in the past week. It's only natural it shed gains today for no fundamental cause," said a city bank trader.
The March also met selling for hedge purposes by a few city banks which earlier paid fixed interest rates in two- and three-year maturities in the swap market, traders said.
Despite the Euroyen's weakness, upward pressure on cash interest rates had subsided by Tuesday.

The scandal-laden Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB) appears to have raised ample cash of up the next month by Tuesday, which is putting mild downward pressure on the money market rates across the spectrum, traders said. DKB's strong demand for raising funds had been underpinning short-term interest rates in the past several weeks, they added.
A total of 11 DKB officials have so far been arrested for suspected involvement in illegal loans to racketeer Ryuichi Koike.

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is expected to impose administrative penalties on DKB, but a MOF source said late last week it would be difficult to impose penalties that affected the bank's core lending and deposit-taking business.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from its regular money market operation at 0020 GMT, leaving the market with a projected surplus of 10 billion yen.
The key overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.50 percent, unchanged from Monday.
The key call rate's failure to rise despite the BOJ's less accomodative credit stance suggested that few people were in a rush to raise funds in the market.
Key three-month certificates of deposit were traded at 0.67 percent, unchanged from Monday.
